title: 《楼上没有声音》
english_summary: Every night at nine, the grandmother upstairs sings the same song. Then one night the apartment goes quiet — and the silence tells you something is wrong.
_content_comment: One beat per line, 'NAME：text' with a fullwidth colon. Beat indices are 0-based and are what panels[].bubbles[].beat refers to; INSERTING A LINE MEANS RE-INDEXING THE PANELS.
content:
我住在一个新的地方。
我的房间在三楼。
楼上住着一位奶奶。
每天晚上九点，她都会唱歌。
她的声音不太好听。
但是每天都一样。
我学习的时候，她在唱。
我睡觉的时候，她还在唱。
我想上去看看她。
可能她一个人不开心。
奶奶打开门。
奶奶：对不起，声音太大了吗？
我想了想。
你：没有。我只是想认识你。
她看着我，笑了。
她的房间里有很多照片。
照片里有一个小孩子。
你：这是你的女儿吗？
奶奶：不是，这是我。
奶奶：我以前很喜欢唱歌。
奶奶：现在，我常常忘记很多事。
奶奶：但是我还记得怎么唱。
第二天晚上，九点到了。
楼上没有声音。
九点十分，还是很安静。
我不能学习了。
我一直在听。
你：可能她今天累了。
你：我应该上去看看。
我等了五分钟。
楼上还是没有声音。
我走上四楼。
门开着。
奶奶坐在地上。
她的电话在很远的地方。
我马上给医院打电话。
医生很快来了。
几天以后，奶奶回家了。
晚上九点，楼上又有声音了。
她唱得还是不太好听。
这一次，我也跟着唱。
奶奶：你也没有唱好。
我们都笑了。
楼上又安静了。
但是我不再害怕安静。
english_content:
I live in a new place.
My room is on the third floor.
A grandmother lives upstairs.
Every night at nine, she sings.
Her voice is not very good.
But it is the same every day.
She sings while I study.
She is still singing when I sleep.
I wanted to go upstairs and see her.
Maybe she is unhappy by herself.
Grandma opened the door.
Sorry, was the sound too loud?
I thought for a moment.
No. I just wanted to meet you.
She looked at me and smiled.
There were many photographs in her room.
There was a little child in one photograph.
Is this your daughter?
No, this is me.
I used to love singing.
Now I often forget many things.
But I still remember how to sing.
The next evening, nine o'clock came.
There was no sound upstairs.
At nine ten, it was still very quiet.
I could not study.
I kept listening.
Maybe she is tired today.
I should go upstairs and look.
I waited five minutes.
There was still no sound upstairs.
I walked up to the fourth floor.
The door was open.
Grandma was sitting on the floor.
Her phone was far away.
I immediately called the hospital.
A doctor came quickly.
A few days later, Grandma came home.
At nine that evening, there was sound upstairs again.
Her singing was still not very good.
This time, I sang along too.
You did not sing well either.
We both laughed.
Upstairs was quiet again.
But I was no longer afraid of the silence.
_vocabulary_comment: Every word is in the cumulative HSK 3 pool (data/hsk2-vocab-snapshot.json + data/hsk3.json). Zero reach words. HSK 3 adds the story's load-bearing words 声音, 安静, 照片, 以前, 忘记 and 应该: the learner can notice a broken routine, understand the past inside the photograph, and decide that silence itself is information.

questions.question: What happened every night at nine?
Who was the little girl in the photograph?
Why did the learner call the hospital?
options: Grandma was on the floor and could not reach her phone

panels.alt: Blue-hour exterior of an older city apartment building, one student arriving with a box while warm windows glow above.
Inside the third-floor room at night, a student looks up toward a ceiling crossed by soft bands of warm sound from upstairs.
Close view of the student at a desk, pencil paused above homework, listening upward with a tired but curious expression.
A quiet split-time composition of the same small room: homework under a desk lamp, then the student awake in bed as the song continues.
On the dim fourth-floor landing, an elderly woman opens a teal apartment door to the student standing in the hall.
The grandmother smiles inside a warm, modest apartment whose walls and shelves hold decades of small framed photographs.
Close-up of an old black-and-white photograph held between young and elderly hands, showing a little girl singing on a simple stage.
The grandmother sits beneath her photographs, one hand over her heart and the other touching the old picture, remembering.
The student waits at the desk beneath a round wall clock near nine, the ceiling above now empty of the familiar warm sound.
Close view of the student frozen over unfinished homework, head tilted toward the silent ceiling as concern replaces annoyance.
Five tense minutes pass in the blue room; the wall clock advances while the student keeps staring at the ceiling.
The student hurries up the dark stairwell and finds the grandmother's teal apartment door standing partly open.
Inside the apartment, the grandmother sits awake on the floor beside a chair while the student kneels nearby and reaches for a distant phone.
A few days later, the grandmother returns along the apartment corridor with the student beside her, both smiling in afternoon light.
Warm cutaway through the floor: grandmother singing upstairs while the student sings along below, both visibly off-key and laughing.
Final blue-hour exterior of the apartment building, two warm windows stacked one above the other in a peaceful quiet night.
